daily_narrative.happened: U.S. stocks sold off broadly, with the S&P 500 down 0.9%, Nasdaq 1.0%, and Russell 2000 1.3%, as higher yields, renewed oil-driven inflation pressure, and geopolitical tension around Iran weighed on risk appetite, while cybersecurity names like CRWD, ZS, OKTA, MDB, and NET fell sharply. The move fits a reflation backdrop, with value, quality, energy, and real estate relatively stronger while momentum and growth lagged, consistent with rotation away from high-valuation tech into more defensive and inflation-sensitive areas.
